subject: science
title: KS3 Science - Working Scientifically: Scientific Investigation
description: A KS3 Working Scientifically pack on planning investigations, identifying variables, collecting reliable evidence, choosing graphs, writing conclusions and evaluating methods. The pack focuses on fair tests, safe practical work, data handling and using evidence rather than opinion.
subtitle: Revision practice for planning fair tests, collecting data and evaluating scientific investigations.

data.sentence: A question that can be answered by collecting evidence is a ____ question.
The variable changed by the investigator is the ____ variable.
The variable measured in an investigation is the ____ variable.
data.hint: It depends on what is changed.

data.sentence: Variables kept the same are called ____ variables.
data.hint: They help make the test fair.

data.sentence: A fair test changes only one ____ variable.
data.hint: Only one main factor should be changed.

data.sentence: A numbered set of detailed practical instructions is called a ____.
data.hint: It explains what to do step by step.

data.sentence: The original measurements collected during an investigation are called ____ data.
A result that does not fit the pattern is an ____.
data.hint: It should be checked, not automatically deleted.

data.sentence: A mean is calculated by adding values and ____ by the number of values.
The smallest change an instrument can measure is its ____.
data.hint: For example, 1 mm on a ruler.

data.sentence: How close a measurement is to the true value is called ____.
data.hint: It is not the same as precision.

data.sentence: How close repeated measurements are to each other is called ____.
data.hint: Close repeats may still be inaccurate.

data.sentence: Results are more ____ when repeated results are consistent and the method is suitable.
A line graph is usually used when the independent variable is ____ numerical data.
A bar chart is usually used when the independent variable is a ____.
The independent variable usually goes on the ____-axis of a graph.
The dependent variable usually goes on the ____-axis of a graph.
A best-fit line shows the overall ____ and does not need to join every point.
A conclusion should use numerical ____ from the results.
data.hint: It should not be based on guesses.

data.sentence: An evaluation should name a specific weakness, explain its effect and suggest an ____.
Hot water is a hazard because it could cause burns or ____.
In the sugar investigation, the same mass of sugar is a ____ variable.
data.hint: It must stay the same for a fair test.

data.title: Stages of a Scientific Investigation
data.instruction: Put the main investigation stages in a sensible order.
items: Ask a testable question.
Make a prediction or hypothesis.
Identify the variables.
Plan a fair and safe method.
Collect repeat results.
Record and process the data.
Write a conclusion and evaluate the method.

data.title: Planning a Toy Car Ramp Test
data.instruction: Put the ramp investigation method in the correct order.
items: Set up the ramp and mark the start line.
Set the ramp height to the first value.
Place the same car at the marked start position.
Release the car without pushing it.
Measure the distance travelled from the start line.
Repeat three times at the same height.
Change only the ramp height and repeat the method.

data.title: Handling an Anomalous Result
data.instruction: Put the best response to an anomaly in the correct order.
items: Notice that one result does not fit the pattern.
Check whether there was an obvious problem during the trial.
Repeat the measurement if possible.
Compare the repeated result with the pattern.
Only exclude the anomaly if there is a clear reason.
Explain the decision in the evaluation.

data.title: Writing a Strong Conclusion
data.instruction: Put the parts of an evidence-based conclusion in order.
items: Answer the original question.
Describe the overall pattern.
Support the pattern with numerical evidence.
Give a scientific explanation if possible.
Mention anomalies or limitations if relevant.
